headline: Single-cell and spatial omics methods impose structure on noisy measurements
label: Single Cell Spatial Omics Methods
summary: Multi-slice spatial atlases and million-cell pretrained models make structure-aware integration of spatial and single-cell data a practical need.
synthesis: The common thread is structure imposed on spatial and single-cell measurements to separate biological programs from technical or confounding variation. SORT couples orthogonality and graph total-variation regularization to matrix factorization to recover multilevel spatial gene programs, while DeSPA uses linear mixed models to detect cross-state spatial remodeling across multi-slice atlases. SCOTE computes scale-resolved spatial covariance tensors across platforms, and Cis-TERN and CellDiffusion use graph constructions to infer pseudotime and align cells across batches. The newer element is spatial and cross-modal factorization built on explicit regularization or covariance geometry, alongside benchmarking and bias-quantification work: a multi-platform sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics benchmark and a count-model framework for imaging spatial transcriptomics technical biases. Other items, including the CellNet pretrained model and histology-conditioned expression prediction, address scale and modality bridging rather than the same problem.
